A. Mole
B. Kelvin
C. Coulomb
D. Ampere

2.text_clean:
2. An object is dropped from rest. Air resistance is not negligible. What is the acceleration of the object at the start of the motion?
A. Zero
B. Increasing
C. Decreasing
D. Constant

3.text_clean:
3. Which of the following is proportional to the net external force acting on a body?
A. Speed
B. Velocity
C. Rate of change of speed
D. Rate of change of velocity

4.text_clean:
4. A small positively charged sphere is suspended from a thread and placed close to a negatively charged rod. When the thread is at 45° to the vertical the system is in equilibrium. The weight of the sphere is $W$ and the magnitude of the electrostatic force between the rod and the sphere is $F$.
[Diagram: positively charged sphere hanging on a thread at 45° to the vertical; horizontal force F towards a negatively charged rod, weight W downwards (not to scale)]
What is the magnitude of $W$ compared with the magnitude of $F$?
A. $W=\sqrt{2}F$
B. $F<W<\sqrt{2}F$
C. $W=F$
D. $W>F$

5.text_clean:
5. A heat engine does 300 J of work during one cycle. In this cycle 900 J of energy is wasted. What is the efficiency of the engine?
A. 0.25
B. 0.33
C. 0.50
D. 0.75

6.text_clean:
6. A student throws a stone with velocity $v$ at an angle $\theta$ to the vertical from the surface of a lake. Air resistance can be ignored. The acceleration due to gravity is $g$.
[Diagram: student at lake surface throwing a stone upwards at angle θ to the vertical]
What is the time taken for the stone to hit the surface of the lake?
A. $\frac{v\sin\theta}{g}$
B. $\frac{v\cos\theta}{g}$
C. $\frac{2v\sin\theta}{g}$
D. $\frac{2v\cos\theta}{g}$

7.text_clean:
7. When 1800 J of energy is supplied to a mass $m$ of liquid in a container, the temperature of the liquid and the container changes by 10 K. When the mass of the liquid is doubled to $2m$, 3000 J of energy is required to change the temperature of the liquid and container by 10 K. What is the specific heat capacity of the liquid in J kg$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$?
A. $\frac{60}{m}$
B. $\frac{120}{m}$
C. $\frac{180}{m}$
D. $\frac{240}{m}$

8.text_clean:
8. An ideal gas and a solid of the same substance are at the same temperature. The average kinetic energy of the gas molecules is $E_g$ and the average kinetic energy of the solid molecules is $E_s$. What is the comparison between $E_g$ and $E_s$?
A. $E_g$ is less than $E_s$.
B. $E_g$ equals $E_s$.
C. $E_g$ is greater than $E_s$.
D. The relationship between $E_g$ and $E_s$ cannot be determined.

[Graph: pressure / $10^5$ Pa (0-6) against volume / m$^3$ (0-6); A at (1, 5), B at (4, 5), C at (1, 2); A→B horizontal at constant pressure, B→C curve, C→A vertical]
What is the work done in joules during the change AB?
A. $15\times10^5$
B. $9.0\times10^5$
C. $4.5\times10^5$
D. 0

10.text_clean:

Entropy change of system | Temperature change of room
A. decreases | decreases
B. decreases | increases
C. increases | decreases
D. increases | increases

A. $2x_0$
B. $x_0$
C. $\lambda$
D. $\frac{\lambda}{2}$

What is the position of the marker at $t=\frac{1}{4f}$?
[Diagram: sinusoidal wave travelling to the right; marker on the equilibrium line between a crest (left) and a trough (right); option positions A directly above the marker at crest height, B directly below at trough depth, C at the trough, D at the next equilibrium crossing]

[Diagram: string fixed between two walls vibrating in three loops (4 nodes)]
How many nodes will be on the string if the frequency is doubled but nothing else is changed?
A. 2
B. 3
C. 7
D. 8

14.text_clean:
14. A source emits sound of wavelength $\lambda_0$ and wave speed $v_0$. A stationary observer hears the sound as the source moves away. What are the wavelength of the sound and the wave speed of the sound as measured by the stationary observer?
Wavelength | Wave speed
A. less than $\lambda_0$ | equal to $v_0$
B. greater than $\lambda_0$ | equal to $v_0$
C. less than $\lambda_0$ | less than $v_0$
D. greater than $\lambda_0$ | less than $v_0$

A. Much less than 0.25 m
B. Between 0.10 m and 0.40 m
C. Equal to 0.25 m
D. Much greater than 0.25 m

The images of the galaxies are just resolved by the telescope. What is the angle subtended by the galaxies at the telescope?
A. 0.05 rad
B. 0.3 rad
C. 5 rad
D. 30 rad

When V is equal to the Brewster angle, which angle is equal to 90°?
A. V + W
B. W only
C. X + Y
D. Z only

Resistance of lamp / Ω | Resistance of diode / Ω

C. 0.50 | 0.25
D. 0.50 | 0.50

A. $R$
B. $2R$
C. $4R$
D. $8R$

A. 0.1 V
B. 1 V
C. 10 V
D. 100 V

B. 1.5 A
C. 1.0 A
D. 0.75 A

A. $\frac{r_M}{r_S}$.
B. $\frac{r_S}{r_M}$.
C. $\frac{r_S^2}{r_M^2}$.
D. $\frac{r_M^2}{r_S^2}$.
